title: The Seriousness of Sins in Islam
summary: The hadith highlights how believers view sins as grave, unlike non-believers.
translation: A hadith emphasizes the seriousness and weight of sins, depicting that a believer sees sins as if they are a mountain about to fall on them, whereas a non-believer considers them as insignificant as a fly on their nose which they easily dismiss. In this hadith, narrated by Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), he stated that people commit deeds which they view as trivial, lighter than a hair, whereas during the time of the Prophet (peace be upon him) we used to consider those acts as destructive. This shows that fear of Allah leads to a fear of sins, and as the fear diminishes, a person becomes bolder in committing them. Companions of the Prophet had intense fear of Allah, making them cautious of even the smallest sin. Furthermore, the closer they were to the Prophet, the higher their level of fear and caution. However, as the era of the Prophet becomes more distant, this state is fading away, which is why Anas indicated that sins considered destructive in their time are viewed as insignificant now. This implies that cultivating fear of Allah in one's heart is crucial as it leads to distancing oneself from sins.
